html:
Alashiya was the Bronze Age kingdom of Cyprus, known from letters of its kings to the pharaohs, which shipped copper across the eastern Mediterranean from about 1600 to 1100 BCE.

Copper from the island's Troodos mountains was cast into heavy ingots shaped like an ox hide, found from Sardinia to the Uluburun shipwreck off Turkey. In the Amarna letters, the king of Alashiya calls the pharaoh his brother and sends him copper. Enkomi, near Famagusta, was a rich port with copper workshops. Mycenaean Greeks settled on the island as the Bronze Age world collapsed around 1200 BCE. The Latin word for copper, cuprum, comes from the Roman name of Cyprus.
sum: Alashiya was the Bronze Age kingdom of Cyprus, known from letters of its kings to the pharaohs, which shipped copper across the eastern Mediterranean from about 1600 to 1100 BCE.
